title: Detection of etaleness through a representable source cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ and representable maps in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A representable map is etale, respectively surjective, if every scheme base change is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], respectively surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces is called chartwise etale if $f\circ a:h_W\to Y$ is representable etale for every representable etale $a:h_W\to X$ with $W$ a scheme. (1) Let $Y$ be an algebraic space, $W,V$ $S$-schemes, $q:h_W\to Y$ a morphism, and $p:V\to W$ a surjective etale scheme morphism. If $q\circ h_p$ is representable etale, then $q$ is representable etale. (2) Let $X,Y,R$ be algebraic spaces, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism and $p:R\to X$ a representable surjective etale morphism. If $f\circ p$ is representable etale, then $f$ is chartwise etale. The source $R$ need not be a scheme. (3) For every representable surjective etale atlas $p:h_U\to X$ with $U$ an $S$-scheme, $f$ is chartwise etale if and only if $f\circ p$ is representable etale. Such an atlas exists for every $X$. All fibre products are the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with scheme fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: For (1), represent the scheme test of q by A using scheme-source representability in [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. That node makes h_p representable surjective etale. Test h_p over A to obtain B with an etale projection d:B→A. The separately supplied surjective test gives the same property for d: any two representing pullback squares are uniquely isomorphic, Yoneda lifts this isomorphism to schemes, and surjectivity is invariant under isomorphisms. Paste the test of h_p with the test of q. The resulting square tests h_p followed by q, so the same uniqueness argument gives etaleness of B→A→T from the hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] to obtain etaleness of A→T. This constructs every test required by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03EC (lemma-etale-over-space), proof of (3), with descent.tex Tag 036W (lemma-etale-etale-local-source) for the scheme-source cancellation.

proof.text: For (2), take the etale scheme test of the representable cover p:R→X along a:h_W→X, obtaining a scheme V, d:V→W and b:h_V→R. Transfer surjectivity from the surjective scheme test to this test by uniqueness of representing squares, as in step 1. To prove b etale, base change the etale scheme-test predicate of a along p: for a scheme test, represent the outer rectangle, use the existing pullback universal property to lift its map, and cancel the right pullback square. This directly proves representable base-change stability from [def-trf-algebraic-space], with no algebraic-space fibre-product construction. Compose b with p followed by f using isEtale_comp of that definition module. The pullback equation identifies this with h_d followed by a followed by f. Apply step 1 to descend to a followed by f. The proof applies to arbitrary presheaf sources and hence does not require R to be a scheme.

source.place: Tag 03FS (lemma-etale-local), source pullback argument of (4) implies (1), using Tag 03EC (3); the same argument uses an arbitrary representable source cover.

proof.text: For (3), choose an atlas $p:h_U\to X$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space], which states its existence and representable surjective etaleness. If $f$ is chartwise etale, apply its defining condition to the chart $p$ to see that $f\circ p$ is representable etale. Conversely, if $f\circ p$ is representable etale, apply (2), proved in Step 2, with $R=h_U$. Thus the equivalence holds for every such atlas, and one exists for every $X$.

lean.statement: theorem etale_source_atlas_detection {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (W V : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj W ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (p : V ⟶ W), Etale p.left → Surjective p.left → IsEtale (yoneda.map p ≫ q) → IsEtale q) ∧ (∀ (X Y R : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : R ⟶ X), IsEtale p.hom.hom → IsSurjective p.hom.hom → IsEtale (p.hom.hom ≫ f.hom.hom) → ∀ (W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → IsEtale (a ≫ f.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale p → IsSurjective p → ((∀ (W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → IsEtale (a ≫ f.hom.hom)) ↔ IsEtale (p ≫ f.hom.hom))) ∧ (∀ X : AlgebraicSpace S, ∃ (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale p ∧ IsSurjective p)
lean.note: The four conjuncts give clauses (1), (2), (3), and atlas existence. Chartwise etaleness is expanded verbatim as its scheme-chart condition, without redefining the existing downstream IsChartwiseEtale or introducing a dependency cycle.
